title: Driver slams car into Wasilla Police Department headquarters
text:
No one inside the building was injured by the crash, officials said Wednesday evening.
A black sedan sits in the doorway of the Wasilla Police Department headquarters after its driver crashed into the building Wednesday, May 13. WASILLA — A man driving a black sedan slammed the vehicle into the entrance of the Wasilla Police Department headquarters late Wednesday afternoon, breaking through one set of doors and stopping in an entryway before he was apprehended by police stationed in the facility.
No one inside the building was injured by the crash, Wasilla Police Department spokesperson Amanda Graham said in an interview. One member of the public was in the lobby at the time of the incident, and a civilian employee was sitting at a reception desk just inside the entryway, she said. The man, whose name was not immediately released, drove around a concrete barrier, across a lawn, and into the doors at about 4:45 p.m., Graham said.
His vehicle did not breach a second set of doors between the entryway and the building’s reception area. Wasilla police and Alaska State Troopers responded immediately and removed the man from the vehicle, Graham said in a statement. He was found to have “insignificant injuries” and was taken into custody, the statement said. A Wasilla Police Department vehicle blocks a bike path that runs parallel to the Wasilla Police Department headquarters Wednesday, May 13.
The area was not secure as of about 6 p.m., Wasilla Police Chief William Rapson said in an interview at the scene. Officials were waiting for a specialized unit from Anchorage to confirm the area was safe, Graham said in the statement. The field was scheduled to host a varsity championship softball game between Wasilla and Colony high schools shortly after 5 p.m., Wasilla High School Principal Jason Marvel said in an interview.
The game has not been rescheduled, he said.
